kept.name: Consecutive Close-Above-Prior-High Exhaustion
kept.note: Counts consecutive bars whose close exceeds the PREVIOUS bar's high -- a strictly stiffer test than an up close, since the whole prior range was engulfed -- and shorts the first bar the streak reaches its threshold, optionally only beneath a 200 EMA. One entry per streak: the signal fires on the bar the counter crosses the threshold and never while it merely stays there. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low.
kept.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1601-1700/1601_Consecutive_Close_High1_Mean_Reversion -- 'counts consecutive closes above the prior high and sells once the count reaches a threshold; position exits when price falls below the prior low; optional 200 EMA filter'

kept.name: Strong Close Into a New Low
kept.note: Shorts the bar that breaks to a new N-bar low and then closes in the top of its own range (IBS above threshold) -- a failed flush whose bounce is already spent by the close. Optional 200-EMA downtrend filter and an optional intraday session window given in UTC minutes-of-day. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low, which is a bar-versus-bar test rather than an indicator.
kept.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1501-1600/1598_10_Bar_Low_Pullback -- 'Low breaks the previous LowestPeriod bars lowest low; IBS > IbsThreshold (0.85); optional close below EMA200; exit on close below previous low'

kept.name: Bayesian Run-Length Collapse
kept.note: Runs Adams-MacKay Bayesian online change-point detection on log returns with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma conjugate prior, and trades the bar on which the MAP run length COLLAPSES instead of incrementing, gated on the posterior putting more than 30% of its mass on a run of five bars or fewer. Direction is read from the new segment, so the rule is agnostic between continuation and reversal.
kept.source: Adams & MacKay, 'Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection', arXiv:0710.3742 (2007) -- run-length posterior, message-passing recursion, constant hazard.

kept.name: Net-Edge Admission Gate
kept.note: Gates a signal on cost rather than on strength. When the base rule fires (close crossing its EMA) three quantities are formed: the AGK EDGE effective-spread estimate over the trailing est_win OHLC bars as a fraction of price, with the Roll half-spread doubled as the fallback when EDGE is undefined; a square-root impact term y_imp*sigma_20*sqrt(Q/V20); and the conditional expected edge, the median forward h_bars log return over every past bar in the trailing edge_look window on which this same signal fired in this same direction, counting only fires at least h_bars old so the outcome was already observable. The trade is admitted only if the expected edge clears hurdle times the round trip, so the identical signal is accepted on a liquid name and refused on an illiquid one at the same dollar size. Cost enters the entry condition, not the P&L accounting.
kept.source: Ardia, D., Guidotti, E., Kroencke, T.A. (2024), 'Efficient Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Open, High, Low, and Close Prices', Journal of Financial Economics 161:103916 (reference implementation at github.com/eguidotti/bidask); Roll (1984) as restated in Novy-Marx & Velikov, 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), p.4; Toth et al. (2011) square-root law for the impact term.

kept.name: Bertram Cost-Aware OU Band Optimization
kept.note: SINGLE-SYMBOL ADAPTATION of a multi-symbol idea. The harness supplies one symbol, so the cointegrated second leg is replaced by the symbol's own trailing mean log price: x = log(C) - mean(log C, mu_win). Everything that makes the idea distinct is kept. An AR(1) fit of x gives theta = -log(rho) per bar and the stationary sd; entry a and exit m are then jointly chosen over a grid to maximise the RATE (m - a - cost)/E[T_cycle], with E[T] the exact OU first-passage time (pi^0.5/theta)*(F(w_m)-F(w_a)), F(w) = int_0^w e^(s^2)(1+erf s) ds, verified against the ODE it solves. The full cycle is a->m plus m->a, so capital's idle leg is paid for too. Bertram's Sharpe objective is not offered: at a zero risk-free rate it collapses to sqrt(E[T]/Var[T]), which is independent of the return per cycle and therefore ignores the cost term entirely - the rate objective is the one where cost bites. m* comes out well away from zero, which is the whole point.
kept.source: Bertram (2010), 'Analytic Solutions for Optimal Statistical Arbitrage Trading', Physica A 389(11); large-scale test with data-snooping controls in Cummins & Bucca (2012), 'Quantitative Spread Trading on Crude Oil and Refined Products Markets', Quantitative Finance. Trade-cycle decomposition T = T1 + T2 and the return function r(a,m,c) = m - a - c reproduced from Krauss (2015), FAU Discussion Paper 09/2015, section 4.2 (equations 22-24).

cut.name: Haircut Sharpe Position Sizing
cut.note: Ten ordinary candidate rules run side by side. At every recompute their expanding-window Sharpes become single-test t-stats and one-sided p-values, get adjusted for multiplicity by Bonferroni, Holm and BHY against a trial count of `trials`, are inverted back to a haircut Sharpe, and become a continuous weight w = clip(HSR/sr_target, 0, w_max); the traded signal is the sign of the w-weighted vote, so allocation moves continuously with multiple-testing-adjusted significance instead of switching on and off, and a rule whose w hits zero on retire_n consecutive recomputes is retired for good (retire_n=0 lets a rule come back). Sizing proper belongs to the harness, so the paper's risk fraction is expressed as the weight each rule carries in the vote. The trial count is swept over 4/10/40 rather than the paper's 100/578/5000: at intraday sample lengths a multiplicity of 100 haircuts every rule to zero and the family never trades at all, which is Harvey and Liu's point but produces no data.
cut.source: Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2015), 'Backtesting', Journal of Portfolio Management 42(1), 13-28 - the haircut Sharpe ratio and the exact Bonferroni / Holm / BHY adjusted p-value formulas, plus the finding that the haircut is non-linear and that the customary 50% haircut is too punitive for high-Sharpe and too lenient for low-Sharpe strategies. PDF: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.PDF . Companion: Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2014), 'Evaluating Trading Strategies', JPM 40(5), 108-118.

cut.name: Rogers-Satchell Drift Detector
cut.note: Ratio of the UNdemeaned close-to-close variance (expectation sigma^2 + mu^2) to the Rogers-Satchell range variance (drift-free), so DR-1 estimates (drift/vol)^2 per bar with no smoothing constant. Trades in the direction of the N-bar return sum when DR clears the gate and the close is the extreme of the last few bars; exits when DR collapses back into the noise. From Rogers & Satchell (1991).
cut.source: Rogers & Satchell (1991), 'Estimating variance from high, low and closing prices', Annals of Applied Probability 1(4), 504-512 (the drift-independent estimator); Parkinson (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 61-65; Garman & Klass (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 67-78. Estimator comparison and formulas: https://portfoliooptimizer.io/blog/range-based-volatility-estimators-overview-and-examples-of-usage/ and https://macrosynergy.com/research/six-ways-to-estimate-realized-volatility/ . The drift-ratio construction itself is my synthesis from those estimators' bias properties.
cut.cut_reason: in-sample score -0.333 -- it never worked on the window it was tuned on

cut.name: Ariel semi-month exposure split
cut.note: Ariel's month partition, unconditional on price: long from the last trading day of the prior month through the Nth trading day of this one, then short (or flat) until the second-to-last session, flat for one day, repeat. Trading-day indices come from the session calendar -- weekday arithmetic with observed holidays removed -- so no price is used to place a session in its month. The daily hold is expressed as a state signal, which is what a rule with no exit event of its own has to be.
cut.source: Ariel, 'A Monthly Effect in Stock Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 18(1), 1987 - cited from the literature; not re-fetched this session (search budget exhausted). The exact split point (Ariel uses the last day of the prior month plus the first half of the month by trading-day count) is pinned to the 9th trading day here so the rule is unambiguous; sweep it.

cut.name: Gap-Cadence Event Calendar Run-In
cut.note: Reconstructs a recurring event calendar from the symbol's OWN bars: take the largest |open/prev-close - 1| jumps in a trailing window, keep the longest subset whose consecutive spacings all fall inside an admissible band, and forecast the next event at last + median spacing. Go long from entry_off bars before that forecast and exit exit_off bars before it -- always flat across the event itself. Self-falsifying: a forecast date that passes without a jump of stale_mult times the typical detected-event jump retires the symbol until a new event is observed. Spacings are in BARS, not sessions, because the probe data is far shorter than a quarterly cycle; on daily bars the band should be set to the 55-70 session spacing the source specifies, and the staleness reference is the median jump of the events the fit itself found rather than a 250-session median. Candidates are chosen with non-maximum suppression (min_sep bars apart, defaulting to half the low end of the spacing band) so that one violent event cannot occupy several candidate slots with its own neighbouring bars -- the source picks the 12 largest gap SESSIONS, which are distinct by construction.
cut.source: Beaver (1968) on announcement-period return variance and trading volume, cited in Kothari & Warner (2006) footnote 1. Frazzini & Lamont (2007) 'The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume' (NBER WP 13090) for the run-in premium. The gap-cadence reconstruction device itself is a synthesis -- no earnings calendar is available on this feed, so the event dates are inferred from the periodicity of the symbol's own overnight gaps, and the estimator is falsifiable.
cut.cut_reason: in-sample score -0.060 -- it never worked on the window it was tuned on

cut.name: Amihud Illiquidity Reversal
cut.note: Bar-based Amihud lambda: rolling mean of |log return| / dollar volume. Buys when that ratio sits above its own trailing percentile AND price is more than atr_d ATRs below its 20-bar mean -- a decline produced by very little money changing hands. Exits when the ratio falls back under its trailing median, or price reclaims the mean, or the clock runs out. The percentile is a true rolling rank over the trailing window, not a fixed cut.
cut.source: Bar-based Amihud lambda, AFML pp.288-289, implemented as get_bar_based_amihud_lambda in mlfinlab/microstructural_features/second_generation.py - source read from the archived mlfinlab-master.zip at https://github.com/mnewls/MLFINLAB.

cut.name: No Supply No Demand Bar
cut.note: Volume Spread Analysis read of an ABSENCE of participation: a narrow-range bar whose volume undercuts each of the previous two bars, closing in the half of its range that contradicts its own direction, taken only in the matching side of the SMA. Mandatory confirmation on the very next bar (close through the signal bar's extreme on higher volume) turns the qualitative read into a rule.
cut.source: Tom Williams, 'Master the Markets' (Volume Spread Analysis). Operational definition -- up/down bar, narrow spread, volume lower than the previous two bars, close position within the bar, confirming next bar on rising volume -- from tradingsetupsreview.com's VSA guide and atas.net's no-demand/no-supply article. 'Narrow spread' is undefined in both sources and is pinned here to a fraction of the mean range of the five bars before the signal bar.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Naked POC Magnet
cut.note: A real volume-at-price profile is built for each regular-hours session: bins bin_pct percent of the session open wide, every bar's volume spread evenly over the bins its [low, high] covers, and the POC is the midpoint of the fullest bin. A finished session's POC joins a list and stays on it only while it remains NAKED - the moment any later session's range contains that price it is struck off, so membership is a topological fact about the tape rather than a threshold. Between start_min and end_min ET the nearest naked POC above and below the last price are measured in units of the SESSION ATR(14) built from the same profiles; the setup trades toward whichever is nearer, provided it sits between min_atr and max_atr away - close enough to be reachable, far enough to be worth the trip. One trade per level per day. Exit is the level itself, or flat at flat_min ET. The 1.0 x session-ATR stop the idea specifies is carried as st_atr in BAR-ATR units, which is the only stop unit the shared harness has.
cut.source: Market Profile / volume profile lineage (Steidlmayer, CBOT Liquidity Data Bank). Definitions and the naked/virgin POC concept per LuxAlgo concept library, https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/naked-poc/ and https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/point-of-control/ ; profile construction per TradingView docs, https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000502040-volume-profile-indicators-basic-concepts/ . Exact bin widths, ATR gating and the 60-session horizon are the harvesting agent's specification.
